t: Tweet Counts Per Frequency — Bucketing Tweets by Frequency
o: We need a design that stores tweets by name and, on query, splits the inclusive range [startTime, endTime] into fixed-size chunks (60/3600/86400 seconds) and counts tweets per chunk. The last chunk may be shorter. Constraints are tiny: at most 10^4 total calls and ranges of length ≤ 10^4, so even scanning all stored tweets per query is fine. The key observation is that chunk index of a time t is simply floor((t - startTime) / size), so we can bucket tweets directly without sorting.
k: Chunk index for time t is (t - startTime) / chunkSize; the number of chunks is (endTime - startTime) / chunkSize + 1.
Store tweet times in a list per name; on query, filter by range and increment the right bucket — no sorting needed given small constraints.
freq maps to sizes: minute→60, hour→3600, day→86400.

a.i: Keep a hash map from tweet name to list of recorded times. On a query, iterate over all times of that name, skip those outside [startTime, endTime], compute their chunk index, and count into an answer array sized (endTime - startTime)/size + 1. This is simple and easily fits within constraints.
s: Map freq to chunk size: minute=60, hour=3600, day=86400.
Create result array of length (endTime - startTime)//size + 1.
For each stored time t of the name with startTime <= t <= endTime, add 1 to result[(t - startTime)//size].
a.t: O(n) per query where n is the number of tweets for that name; recordTweet is O(1). With ≤10^4 calls this is trivially fast.
a.sp: O(n) to store all tweet times.

a.i: Keep each name's times sorted (insert via binary search or sort lazily). A query then uses two binary searches to find the slice of times inside [startTime, endTime], and only iterates over relevant tweets. This scales better when there are many tweets outside queried ranges.
s: recordTweet: insert time into map[tweetName] keeping it sorted (binary search insertion point).
On query, binary search for the first index with time >= startTime and the first index with time > endTime.
Iterate only over that slice, incrementing result[(t - startTime)//size].
a.t: recordTweet is O(n) due to sorted insertion (amortized); each query is O(log n + k) where k is the number of tweets in range.
a.sp: O(n) to store all tweet times.

w: In an interview, present Approach 1 first — it is clean, obviously correct, and comfortably within constraints; mention Approach 2 as the scaling improvement if queries hit few tweets among many stored ones. Pitfalls: the range is inclusive on both ends (use <= endTime), the number of chunks is (endTime - startTime)//size + 1 (not +2), and duplicate timestamps must be counted individually. Edge cases: single-tweet chunks like [0,59] vs [0,60], and queries before any tweets exist (empty list handling). Follow-ups might ask for streaming/bucketed storage (pre-bucket by absolute time windows) or supporting arbitrary frequencies.
